divinatory_meanings.upright: Between the alternative readings there is no marriage possible; on the one hand, riches, fortune, magnificence; on the other, physical suffering, disease, chagrin, sadness, mortification. The design gives one suggestion; here is a lord overlooking his dominion and alternately contemplating a globe; it looks like the malady, the mortification, the sadness of Alexander amidst the grandeur of this world's wealth.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Surprise, wonder, enchantment, emotion, trouble, fear.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A young lady may expect trivial disappointments.

divinatory_meanings.upright: He symbolizes established strength, enterprise, effort, trade, commerce, discovery; those are his ships, bearing his merchandise, which are sailing over the sea. The card also signifies able co-operation in business, as if the successful merchant prince were looking from his side towards yours with a view to help you.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The end of troubles, suspension or cessation of adversity, toil and disappointment.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A very good card; collaboration will favour enterprise.

divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Unexpected good fortune.

divinatory_meanings.reversed: Litigation, disputes, trickery, contradiction.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Success in financial speculation.

divinatory_meanings.upright: The card has been so designed that it can cover several significations; on the surface, it is a victor triumphing, but it is also great news, such as might be carried in state by the King's courier; it is expectation crowned with its own desire, the crown of hope, and so forth.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Apprehension, fear, as of a victorious enemy at the gate; treachery, disloyalty, as of gates being opened to the enemy; also indefinite delay.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Servants may lose the confidence of their masters; a young lady may be betrayed by a friend.

divinatory_meanings.upright: It is a card of valour, for, on the surface, six are attacking one, who has, however, the vantage position. On the intellectual plane, it signifies discussion, wordy strife; in business—negotiations, war of trade, barter, competition. It is further a card of success, for the combatant is on the top and his enemies may be unable to reach him.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Perplexity, embarrassments, anxiety. It is also a caution against indecision.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A dark child.

divinatory_meanings.reversed: Arrows of jealousy, internal dispute, stingings of conscience, quarrels; and domestic disputes for persons who are married.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Domestic disputes for a married person.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII

divinatory_meanings.upright: The card signifies strength in opposition. If attacked, the person will meet an onslaught boldly; and his build shews that he may prove a formidable antagonist. With this main significance there are all its possible adjuncts—delay, suspension, adjournment.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Obstacles, adversity, calamity.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Generally speaking, a bad card.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII

correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: A card of many significances, and some of the readings cannot be harmonized. I set aside that which connects it with honour and good faith. The chief meaning is oppression simply, but it is also fortune, gain, any kind of success, and then it is the oppression of these things. It is also a card of false-seeming, disguise, perfidy. The place which the figure is approaching may suffer from the rods that he carries. Success is stultified if the Nine of Swords follows, and if it is a question of a lawsuit, there will be certain loss.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Contrarieties, difficulties, intrigues, and their analogies.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Difficulties and contradictions, if near a good card.

divinatory_meanings.reversed: Anecdotes, announcements, evil news. Also indecision and the instability which accompanies it.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Young man of family in search of young lady.

divinatory_meanings.reversed: News, alliances, affinity, consanguinity, ancestry, return, false projects.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Generally favourable; a happy marriage; also patrimony, legacies, gifts, success in enterprise.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Return of some relative who has not been seen for long.

Another reading reverses this, giving new relations, new knowledge, new environment, and then the children are disporting in an unfamiliar precinct.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The future, renewal, that which will come to pass presently.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Pleasant memories.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Fairy favours, images of reflection, sentiment, imagination, things seen in the glass of contemplation; some attainment in these degrees, but nothing permanent or substantial is suggested.

divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Fair child; idea, design, resolve, movement.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Success, if accompanied by the Three of Cups.

divinatory_meanings.upright: The card speaks for itself on the surface, but other readings are entirely antithetical—giving joy, mildness, timidity, honour, modesty. In practice, it is usually found that the card shews the decline of a matter, or that a matter which has been thought to be important is really of slight consequence—either for good or evil.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Great joy, happiness, feasting.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Marriage with a fair woman.

correspondence.title: The Lord of Abandoned Success
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Concord, contentment, physical bien-être; also victory, success, advantage; satisfaction for the Querent or person for whom the consultation is made.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Truth, loyalty, liberty; but the readings vary and include mistakes, imperfections, etc.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Of good augury for military men.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Material Happiness
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Contentment, repose of the entire heart; the perfection of that state; also perfection of human love and friendship; if with several picture-cards, a person who is taking charge of the Querent's interests; also the town, village or country inhabited by the Querent.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Repose of the false heart, indignation, violence.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: For a male Querent, a good marriage and one beyond his expectations.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Perfected Success
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Fair young man, one impelled to render service and with whom the Querent will be connected; a studious youth; news, message; application, reflection, meditation; also these things directed to business.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Taste, inclination, attachment, seduction, deception, artifice.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Good augury; also a young man who is unfortunate in love.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Princess of the Waters; the Lotus of the Palace of the Floods
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Arrival, approach—sometimes that of a messenger; advances, proposition, demeanour, invitation, incitement.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Trickery, artifice, subtlety, swindling, duplicity, fraud.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A visit from a friend, who will bring unexpected money to the Querent.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Lord of the Waves and the Waters; the King of the Hosts of the Sea
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Good, fair woman; honest, devoted woman, who will do service to the Querent; loving intelligence, and hence the gift of vision; success, happiness, pleasure; also wisdom, virtue; a perfect spouse and a good mother.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The accounts vary; good woman; otherwise, distinguished woman but one not to be trusted; perverse woman; vice, dishonour, depravity.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Sometimes denotes a woman of equivocal character.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A rich marriage for a man and a distinguished one for a woman.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Queen of the Thrones of the Waters
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Fair man, man of business, law, or divinity; responsible, disposed to oblige the Querent; also equity, art and science, including those who profess science, law and art; creative intelligence.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Dishonest, double-dealing man; roguery, exaction, injustice, vice, scandal, pillage, considerable loss.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Beware of ill-will on the part of a man of position, and of hypocrisy pretending to help.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Prince of the Chariot of the Waters
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Triumph, the excessive degree in everything, conquest, triumph of force. It is a card of great force, in love as well as in hatred. The crown may carry a much higher significance than comes usually within the sphere of fortune-telling.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The same, but the results are disastrous; another account says—conception, childbirth, augmentation, multiplicity.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Great prosperity or great misery.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Marriage broken off, for a woman, through her own imprudence.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Root of the Powers of Air
correspondence.note: An Ace is an elemental root; no single planet or zodiac sign is asserted.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Conformity and the equipoise which it suggests, courage, friendship, concord in a state of arms; another reading gives tenderness, affection, intimacy. The suggestion of harmony and other favourable readings must be considered in a qualified manner, as Swords generally are not symbolical of beneficent forces in human affairs.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Imposture, falsehood, duplicity, disloyalty.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Gifts for a lady, influential protection for a man in search of help.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Peace Restored
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Removal, absence, delay, division, rupture, dispersion, and all that the design signifies naturally, being too simple and obvious to call for specific enumeration.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Mental alienation, error, loss, distraction, disorder, confusion.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: For a woman, the flight of her lover.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A meeting with one whom the Querent has compromised; also a nun.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Sorrow
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Vigilance, retreat, solitude, hermit's repose, exile, tomb and coffin. It is these last that have suggested the design.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Wise administration, circumspection, economy, avarice, precaution, testament.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A bad card, but if reversed a qualified success may be expected by wise administration of affairs.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A certain success following wise administration.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Rest from Strife
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Degradation, destruction, revocation, infamy, dishonour, loss, with the variants and analogues of these.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The same; burial and obsequies.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: An attack on the fortune of the Querent.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A sign of sorrow and mourning.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Defeat
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Journey by water, route, way, envoy, commissionary, expedient.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Declaration, confession, publicity; one account says that it is a proposal of love.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: The voyage will be pleasant.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Earned Success
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Design, attempt, wish, hope, confidence; also quarrelling, a plan that may fail, annoyance. The design is uncertain in its import, because the significations are widely at variance with each other.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Good advice, counsel, instruction, slander, babbling.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Dark girl; a good card; it promises a country life after a competence has been secured.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Unstable Effort
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Bad news, violent chagrin, crisis, censure, power in trammels, conflict, calumny; also sickness.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Disquiet, difficulty, opposition, accident, treachery; what is unforeseen; fatality.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: For a woman, scandal spread in her respect.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Shortened Force
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Death, failure, miscarriage, delay, deception, disappointment, despair.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Imprisonment, suspicion, doubt, reasonable fear, shame.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: An ecclesiastic, a priest; generally, a card of bad omen.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Good ground for suspicion against a doubtful person.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Despair and Cruelty
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Whatsoever is intimated by the design; also pain, affliction, tears, sadness, desolation. It is not especially a card of violent death.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Advantage, profit, success, favour, but none of these are permanent; also power and authority.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Followed by Ace and King, imprisonment; for girl or wife, treason on the part of friends.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Victory and consequent fortune for a soldier in war.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Ruin
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Authority, overseeing, secret service, vigilance, spying, examination, and the qualities thereto belonging.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: More evil side of these qualities; what is unforeseen, unprepared state; sickness is also intimated.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: An indiscreet person will pry into the Querent's secrets.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Princess of the Rushing Winds; the Lotus of the Palace of Air
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Skill, bravery, capacity, defence, address, enmity, wrath, war, destruction, opposition, resistance, ruin. There is therefore a sense in which the card signifies death, but it carries this meaning only in its proximity to other cards of fatality.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Imprudence, incapacity, extravagance.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A soldier, man of arms, satellite, stipendiary; heroic action predicted for soldier.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: Dispute with an imbecile person; for a woman, struggle with a rival, who will be conquered.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Lord of the Wind and the Breezes; the King of the Spirits of Air
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Widowhood, female sadness and embarrassment, absence, sterility, mourning, privation, separation.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Malice, bigotry, artifice, prudery, bale, deceit.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A widow.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A bad woman, with ill-will towards the Querent.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Queen of the Thrones of Air
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Whatsoever arises out of the idea of judgment and all its connexions—power, command, authority, militant intelligence, law, offices of the crown, and so forth.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Cruelty, perversity, barbarity, perfidy, evil intention.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A lawyer, senator, doctor.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A bad man; also a caution to put an end to a ruinous lawsuit.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Prince of the Chariot of the Winds
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Perfect contentment, felicity, ecstasy; also speedy intelligence; gold.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: The evil side of wealth, bad intelligence; also great riches. In any case it shews prosperity, comfortable material conditions, but whether these are of advantage to the possessor will depend on whether the card is reversed or not.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: The most favourable of all cards.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A share in the finding of treasure.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Root of the Powers of Earth
correspondence.note: An Ace is an elemental root; no single planet or zodiac sign is asserted.

divinatory_meanings.upright: On the one hand it is represented as a card of gaiety, recreation and its connexions, which is the subject of the design; but it is read also as news and messages in writing, as obstacles, agitation, trouble, embroilment.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Enforced gaiety, simulated enjoyment, literal sense, handwriting, composition, letters of exchange.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Troubles are more imaginary than real.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Harmonious Change
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Métier, trade, skilled labour; usually, however, regarded as a card of nobility, aristocracy, renown, glory.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Mediocrity, in work and otherwise, puerility, pettiness, weakness.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: If for a man, celebrity for his eldest son.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Material Works
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: The surety of possessions, cleaving to that which one has, gift, legacy, inheritance.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Suspense, delay, opposition.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: For a bachelor, pleasant news from a lady.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Earthly Power
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: The card foretells material trouble above all, whether in the form illustrated—that is, destitution—or otherwise. For some cartomancists, it is a card of love and lovers—wife, husband, friend, mistress; also concordance, affinities. These alternatives cannot be harmonized.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Disorder, chaos, ruin, discord, profligacy.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Conquest of fortune by reason.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Material Trouble
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Presents, gifts, gratification; another account says attention, vigilance; now is the accepted time, present prosperity, etc.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Desire, cupidity, envy, jealousy, illusion.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: The present must not be relied on.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A check on the Querent's ambition.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Material Success
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: These are exceedingly contradictory; in the main, it is a card of money, business, barter; but one reading gives altercation, quarrel—and another innocence, ingenuity, purgation.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Improved position for a lady's future husband.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Success Unfulfilled
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Work, employment, commission, craftsmanship, skill in craft and business, perhaps in the preparatory stage.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Voided ambition, vanity, cupidity, exaction, usury. It may also signify the possession of skill, in the sense of the ingenious mind turned to cunning and intrigue.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A young man in business who has relations with the Querent; a dark girl.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: The Querent will be compromised in a matter of money-lending.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Prudence
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, certitude, discernment.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Roguery, deception, voided project, bad faith.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Prompt fulfilment of what is presaged by neighbouring cards.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Material Gain
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Gain, riches; family matters, archives, extraction, the abode of a family.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Chance, fatality, loss, robbery, games of hazard; sometimes gift, dowry, pension.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Represents house or dwelling, and derives its value from other cards.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: An occasion which may be fortunate or otherwise.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII
correspondence.title: The Lord of Wealth
correspondence.note: Golden Dawn decan attribution for numbered Minor Arcana.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Application, study, scholarship, reflection; another reading says news, messages and the bringer thereof; also rule, management.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Prodigality, dissipation, liberality, luxury; unfavourable news.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A dark youth; a young officer or soldier; a child.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Princess of the Echoing Hills; the Rose of the Palace of Earth
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Utility, serviceableness, interest, responsibility, rectitude—all on the normal and external plane.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: inertia, idleness, repose of that kind, stagnation; also placidity, discouragement, carelessness.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: An useful man; useful discoveries.
divinatory_meanings.additional_reversed: A brave man out of employment.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Lord of the Wide and Fertile Land; the King of the Spirits of Earth
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, liberty.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, mistrust.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: Dark woman; presents from a rich relative; rich and happy marriage for a young man.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Queen of the Thrones of Earth
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.

divinatory_meanings.upright: Valour, realizing intelligence, business and normal intellectual aptitude, sometimes mathematical gifts and attainments of this kind; success in these paths.
divinatory_meanings.reversed: Vice, weakness, ugliness, perversity, corruption, peril.
divinatory_meanings.editorial_note: Historical source wording; interpret in context rather than as an empirical prediction.
divinatory_meanings.additional_upright: A rather dark man, a merchant, master, professor.

correspondence.system: Golden Dawn Book T / Liber LXXVIII, mapped to RWS labels
correspondence.title: The Prince of the Chariot of Earth
correspondence.note: Mounted RWS Knight=Fire; Queen=Water; RWS King=Golden Dawn Prince/Air; Page=Earth.
